note: Design-for-Manufacture / Design-for-Assembly rule packs for FDM 3D printing, tuned to a default 0.4 mm nozzle unless 'applies' narrows it. Values are practical defaults a gate can check against; tighten per material/printer. Each entry: { rule, value, unit, applies, note }.

rules.applies: diametral/total gap between two printed parts intended to slide or rotate freely (e.g. pin in bore, shaft in journal); 0.4 mm nozzle
rules.note: Loose running fit. Split this as ~0.2 mm radial per side. Increase if either surface is unfinished or the printer is poorly calibrated.

rules.applies: designed-in gap for a printed-to-printed assembly fit that should locate but still go together by hand; 0.4 mm nozzle
rules.note: The minimum reliable clearance at a 0.4 mm nozzle. The plan's check_printed_fit floor: >=0.2 mm at every printed-to-printed mating joint or it won't assemble.

rules.applies: interference/press fit between printed parts (heat-set insert pocket, pin meant to stay put); 0.4 mm nozzle
rules.note: Slight interference. Below ~0.1 mm the parts effectively fuse / crack on insertion. For heat-set brass inserts, size the pocket to the insert's lead diameter, not the major.

rules.applies: rule of thumb to rescale clearance bands for non-0.4 mm nozzles
rules.note: Approximate the snug clearance as ~0.5x nozzle width (0.2 mm @ 0.4 nozzle, ~0.3 mm @ 0.6 nozzle, ~0.125 mm @ 0.25 nozzle). Larger nozzles need larger clearances.

rules.applies: load-bearing wall / link / bracket on a 0.4 mm nozzle
rules.note: ~5 perimeters at 0.4 mm. Below this, structural parts flex and delaminate at layer lines. Brackets carrying servo/joint loads should derive wall from load (plan S5) but never go under 2 mm.

rules.applies: non-structural shell / cover / fairing on a 0.4 mm nozzle
rules.note: ~3 perimeters. Fine for enclosures that carry no load.

rules.applies: thin standing rib, fin, or vent slat oriented vertically; 0.4 mm nozzle
rules.note: ~2 perimeters. Thinner standing features wobble during printing and won't bond.

rules.applies: wall thickness of material surrounding a screw/insert boss
rules.note: Wall around a tapped/insert hole must be >= ~0.8x the screw nominal and >= 2 mm so the boss doesn't split when the screw is driven.

rules.applies: self-supporting overhang on FDM; angle measured from the vertical (build) axis
rules.note: Up to ~45 deg from vertical prints cleanly without support. Steeper (toward horizontal) needs support or a redesign (chamfer instead of fillet on downward faces).

rules.applies: horizontal unsupported bridge between two anchored points
rules.note: Short bridges (<=~5 mm, generously up to ~10 mm with good cooling) print without support. Longer spans sag — add a support, a center pillar, or split the part.

rules.applies: holes printed with their axis horizontal (parallel to the bed)
rules.note: A round horizontal hole sags at its top; use a teardrop/diamond profile or orient the hole axis vertical so it prints as stacked circles.

rules.applies: thread engagement depth for a bolt into a plastic/printed tapped boss
rules.note: Engage >= 2x the bolt nominal diameter (e.g. >= 6 mm for an M3) in plastic so threads don't strip. Prefer heat-set brass inserts over tapping plastic directly for any repeated assembly.

rules.applies: thread engagement depth for a bolt into aluminum
thread engagement depth for a bolt into steel
blind pocket depth for a heat-set threaded insert
rules.note: Make the pocket ~10% deeper than the insert so displaced plastic has somewhere to go and the insert seats flush. Pocket diameter = insert lead diameter.

rules.applies: through-clearance hole for a bolt shank (not tapped)
rules.note: Clearance hole ~ nominal + 0.5 mm (e.g. 3.5 mm for M3) so the bolt passes freely and pulls the joint tight against the head/nut.

rules.applies: any small printed hole that must hit a target diameter
rules.note: FDM holes print undersize (elephant-foot + inward perimeter pull). Oversize the modeled diameter by ~0.1-0.3 mm or plan to ream/drill.

rules.applies: inside corners on a load-carrying structural part
rules.note: Add a >= 1 mm fillet to interior corners in the load path; sharp internal corners are stress risers that crack under cyclic joint load. (Plan S6 surface gate.)

rules.applies: clearance between a servo can and the pocket/shell that encloses it
rules.note: Leave >= 2 mm around an enclosed servo body for cooling and tolerance; don't print a zero-gap pocket. Pairs with the pattern-card vent strategy.
